sections.title: How to use this guide
sections.intro: This page is assembled only from the facts stored in the nodes, so every claim below can be traced back to a lecture or lab slide.

items.text: Read it top to bottom once: the map shows the whole course, the reference sheet gives the must-know definitions, the niche sheet gives small numbers and names, the traps sheet shows where marks are lost, then the checklist and the core-first route close the loop.

Cram mode follows the core-first route: 44 core nodes in teaching order, about 320 min (5 h 20) in total, then the traps and the night-before checklist. Choose it when time is short and you need the headline concepts first.

Mastery mode follows the main pathway stage by stage through all 122 nodes (core, standard and detail), about 786 min (13 h 06). Choose it when you have days, want every small fact, and want to see how each idea leads to the next.

sections.title: The course map
sections.intro: The main pathway is the professor's own teaching order: 10 stages, 122 nodes. Each stage groups nodes taught together.

items.text: Stage 1, Course frame, the relational baseline and why NoSQL - 18 nodes, 9 core, about 98 min. Lecture 1 opens with prerequisites and the framing scenarios, recalls Codd, anomalies and the RDBMS, then moves to JSON formats, the NoSQL definition, motivations and trade-offs.

Stage 2, TP1: designing and querying a relational schema - 9 nodes, 2 core, about 62 min. TP1 follows Lecture 1 with the University of Atlas case, from schema design and DDL to inserts, joins and aggregation.

sections.title: Must-know definitions and rules
sections.intro: One line each. If you can say these aloud without looking, you cover the headline questions of a lesson-based final.

items.text: An RDBMS has four core components: storage management, memory management, the data dictionary and a query language (SQL).
items.quote: Inside an RDBMS: Four Core Components

items.text: NoSQL stores and retrieves data without the tabular relations of relational databases, and is used in real-time web applications and big data.
items.quote: Used in real-time web applications and big data.

items.text: The core trade-off: relational gives more functionality (schema first, mature consistency); NoSQL gives less functionality but is easy to scale and much faster for most operations.
items.quote: A key advantage of NoSQL is that it is easy to scale and much faster for most operations.

sections.title: Traps and look-alikes
sections.intro: Places where two ideas look alike or an obvious answer is incomplete. Each one points back to the slide that settles it.

items.text: Trap: NoSQL does not simply mean "no SQL"; it is sometimes called "Not only SQL" to stress that these systems may support SQL-like query languages.
items.quote: Sometimes called “Not only SQL” to emphasize that they may support SQL-like query languages.

items.text: Trap: the word consistency has two meanings in the lectures, transaction consistency and replica consistency; the slide warns not to confuse them.
Trap: CAP is not "pick any two" in practice; partitions are rare on local networks, so designers mostly trade consistency against availability.
items.quote: In practice, partitions are rare on local networks

sections.title: Night-before checklist
sections.intro: No new material tonight. Re-read, say aloud, then sleep.

items.text: Re-read the reference sheet once, slowly, then cover it and say each definition aloud in one sentence.
Re-read the niche facts sheet in lecture order and write the numbers and names from memory on a blank page: dates, thresholds, port-like figures, product limits.
Say aloud: the CAP trio and the two meanings of consistency; the four ACID and three BASE properties; read and write thresholds with 5 replicas.

sections.title: Core-first route
sections.intro: The 44 core nodes in main-pathway order, about 320 min (5 h 20) in total. Do these first; anything else is a bonus.

items.text: Different requirements, different databases - sets the idea behind the whole course: requirements decide the structure, bank transfer versus shopping cart (about 5 min)
JSON: format, properties and syntax rules - JSON is the document format used for the rest of the course and a likely recall question (about 7 min)
What NoSQL is - the base definition every other answer builds on, including the named examples (about 5 min)
When to choose NoSQL - the checklist for choosing NoSQL, the typical scenario question (about 5 min)
